answer_text:
Let

\[
a_1=\sqrt{\frac12},\qquad a_{n+1}=\sqrt{\frac12+\frac12 a_n}.
\]

Then the product is

\[
P=a_1a_2a_3\cdots=\prod_{n=1}^\infty a_n.
\]

Using the half-angle identity

\[
\cos\frac{x}{2}=\sqrt{\frac{1+\cos x}{2}},
\]

we observe

\[
a_1=\sqrt{\frac12}=\cos\frac{\pi}{4}.
\]

If \(a_n=\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2^{n+1}}\right)\), then

\[
a_{n+1}
=\sqrt{\frac{1+\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2^{n+1}}\right)}{2}}
=\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2^{n+2}}\right).
\]

Thus

\[
a_n=\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2^{n+1}}\right),
\]

and so

\[
P=\prod_{n=1}^\infty \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2^{n+1}}\right).
\]

Now use the repeated double-angle identity

\[
\sin x
=
2^N\sin\left(\frac{x}{2^N}\right)
\prod_{n=1}^N \cos\left(\frac{x}{2^n}\right).
\]

Take \(x=\frac{\pi}{2}\). Then

\[
1=\sin\frac{\pi}{2}
=
2^N\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2^{N+1}}\right)
\prod_{n=1}^N \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2^{n+1}}\right).
\]

Therefore the \(N\)-th partial product is

\[
P_N=
\frac{1}{2^N\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2^{N+1}}\right)}.
\]

As \(N\to\infty\),

\[
2^N\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2^{N+1}}\right)
\to
2^N\cdot \frac{\pi}{2^{N+1}}
=
\frac{\pi}{2}.
\]

Hence

\[
P=\frac{2}{\pi}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{2}{\pi}}
\]
